lessons_learned.observation: Without closing prices we cannot measure whether the leadership-change catalyst produced any excess return relative to the broader market
lessons_learned.adjustment: Require closing-price confirmation before declaring any catalyst trade complete

lessons_learned.observation: The launch catalyst produced no sustained follow-through once broader market volatility from geopolitical headlines took over
lessons_learned.adjustment: Require both a fundamental catalyst and a volume spike above the 20-day average before committing capital to healthcare launches

lessons_learned.observation: The valuation setup delivered modest stability on a down day for growth indices, showing that depressed multiples can act as a buffer when momentum names rotate
lessons_learned.adjustment: Pair valuation screens with a same-day volume check before treating any rebound as confirmed

lessons_learned.observation: The earnings-driven momentum entry worked because data-center demand exceeded expectations and sector rotation supported the move
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always require volume confirmation above the 20-day average before entering momentum trades on earnings beats

lessons_learned.observation: Capturing a modest same-day gain validated quick execution on cross-asset signals, yet the portfolio’s persistent underperformance versus the NASDAQ underscores how difficult it remains to generate consistent alpha with single-day volatile assets
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always cross-check crypto price feeds with at least two independent sources before executing flash trades

lessons_learned.observation: Capturing a modest gain on the BTC flash trade validated the use of cross-asset signals for opportunistic entries, but the underperformance relative to the NASDAQ underscores the difficulty of beating broad indices on single-day volatile assets. The key adjustment is strengthening confirmation criteria to ensure the signal has substance beyond initial movement
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always verify price data from multiple providers before entering a flash trade on volatile assets like crypto

lessons_learned.observation: The bid-ask-spread / order-flow-slippage lesson was taught in 6 of 8 recent episodes with nearly identical framing. Listeners tuned out after the third repeat.
lessons_learned.adjustment: Never re-teach bid_ask_spread or order_flow_slippage within their 45-day cooldown. If the only interesting mechanic today is a stale one, pick a different mechanic — freshness beats any single lesson.

lessons_learned.observation: The last 10 picks skewed 35% toward precious metals (Fortuna, SSR, West Red Lake) with zero flag raised on air. A real portfolio would have rebalanced.
lessons_learned.adjustment: Cap any single sector at 30% of the trailing 10-trade window. When the sector-concentration warning fires, the Practice Investment MUST pick a different sector that episode.

lessons_learned.observation: No episode has ever named the portfolio's alpha versus the NASDAQ Composite. Listeners have no way to judge whether the show is beating the market.
lessons_learned.adjustment: Every episode must state NASDAQ Composite level, portfolio YTD return, and YTD alpha in the Market Pulse segment. Fridays add the weekly alpha. Monthly episodes add month-to-date alpha.

lessons_learned.observation: Quick Hits consistently slipped into pure news reading (maple syrup shortage, Ackman's Universal Music bid, craft-brewer cost absorption) with no investing angle.
lessons_learned.adjustment: Every Quick Hit ends with an **Action:** line containing exactly one concrete portfolio decision stated as a verb phrase. Items without a concrete action are rejected at the digest stage.
